high_value_findings: OpenASR q8 is a distinct challenger, not a proven quantization of the current F2 Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B-hf baseline: OpenASR declares Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B as its conversion source, and the two current official Qwen model artifacts have different surfaced sizes and SHA-256 identities.

OpenASR's registry explicitly includes German and defaults the published 0.6B pack to q8_0; upstream reports approximately 1.01 GB pack and 2.86 GB isolated RAM peak, but those performance/quantization numbers are M1/JFK source evidence only.

OpenASR's own Qwen audit verifies CPU/Metal on its cited M1 evidence while marking CUDA/Vulkan/HIP untested for this family; target hardware/backend correctness must precede any performance credit on those paths.
OpenASR runtime development is moving rapidly in GPU residency/KV/decode/resource admission; any F2 test must pin exact runtime build/commit and model pack digest rather than use latest.
continuation: Do not duplicate the active hardware-roundtrip claim. When its real hardware receipt lands, decide CPU versus verified target backend before opening a separate OpenASR E3 benchmark claim.
